Just curious, and I'm sure this question has been asked already and it's my failure to find it with the search function, but what is the ultimate damage type that Mr. Fixer outputs when you use Tire Iron and Grease Monkey Fist?  Tire Iron says his damage type turns into projectile. Again, apologies if I'm missing the answer on the board already. I may have had a herp derp moment with the search function here.

posts.name: Medic-Tank
posts.cooked:
Let's break it down in pieces classic play was apply the cards in the order they are played thus the damage type used to always be projectile if Tire Iron came out in second and your choice if Grease Monkey Fist was out second. But that's all in the past.

Now, both of those cards change damage type and well one would argue that trying to change the damage type occurs at the same time, thus by the OoO (Order of Operations ruling) you get to choose wich happens first. You now get to imagine your strike going from melee to range as it flies with the tire iron and the burst in flames if you like classic types or simply go with Rainbow Unicorn Lunar type of damage if it floats your boat. You also get the option of simply applying it in the order they fell on the table if you feel better this way cause in the end the choice is yours. The key component is to have fun...

Actually I believe that Order of Operations never affected this question.

 

Optional damage changes happen after static changes.

If Imbued Fire and Cramped Quarters combat are both out th players don't decide which to use, the last one to ener play overwrites the previous ones.

 

Static effects do not have timing, therefore they cannot activate Order rulings.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Static Effects do not have timing.  That is still official.  It has never been overruled.

It was also ruled that the last static change card is the one that you go by.

 

We also know that for cards entering play you can't choose to have an effect destroy Informant before her response activates.  So no, everything is not player choice.

Twist the Ether is an optional effect.  it can activate at any time that is a valid time to activate.  Anytime during the damage dealing process is valid, therefore Twist the ehter can activate at any time during that process.  So it never had to do with order of entering play.

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
phantaskippy:

Static Effects do not have timing.  That is still official.  It has never been overruled.

Sure it has. The exact moment when Christopher put up the new Order of Operations rule, which supercedes every notion of "static effect" any of us ever had.

Those static effects are simultaneous effects, as defined by how Fort/SHD interact under the OoO. 

You have to stop using "static effects". Its confusing and overly complicated when the OoO ruling was specifically put in place to make these questions easy. 

All simultaneous effects (save Start/End turn) are handled by player choice. Static Effects were always considered simultaneous, even before the OoO, we just didn't know how to handle them correctly. Now we do.
